stem: What is the typical female-to-male ratio in developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)?
explanation: Female predominance is a classic feature of developmental dysplasia of the hip, with an approximate female-to-male ratio of 6:1.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this underestimates the usual female predominance seen in developmental dysplasia of the hip.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this ratio is lower than the commonly observed female-to-male ratio in developmental dysplasia of the hip.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because developmental dysplasia of the hip has a strong female predominance, with an approximate female-to-male ratio of 6:1.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because this overstates the typical female-to-male ratio reported for developmental dysplasia of the hip.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this is higher than the usual female-to-male ratio in developmental dysplasia of the hip.

source.hint: The source material mentions a very strong predilection for females compared to males.
